arxiv-2104-08216.title: Local and scalable detection of genuine multipartite single-photon path entanglement
arxiv-2104-08216.creator: Patrik Caspar, Enky Oudot, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Maring, Anthony Martin, Nicolas Sangouard, Hugo Zbinden, Rob Thew
arxiv-2104-08216.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Patrik Caspar, Enky Oudot, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Maring, Anthony Martin, Nicolas Sangouard, Hugo Zbinden, Rob Thew. How can a multipartite single-photon path-entangled state be certified efficiently by means of local measurements? We address this question by constructing an entanglement witness based on local photon detections preceded by displacement operations to reveal genuine multipartite entanglement. Our witness is defined as a sum of three observables that can be measured locally and assessed with two measurement settings for any number of parties N N .

arxiv-2106-16235.title: Unbiasing Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo with a Quantum Computer
arxiv-2106-16235.creator: William J. Huggins, Bryan A. O’Gorman, Nicholas C. Rubin, David R. Reichman, Ryan Babbush, Joonho Lee
arxiv-2106-16235.description: Abstract Many-electron problems pose some of the greatest challenges in computational science, with important applications across many fields of modern science. Fermionic quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods are among the most powerful approaches to these problems. However, they can be severely biased when controlling the fermionic sign problem using constraints, as is necessary for scalability.

arxiv-2205-07084.title: Short-Pulsed Metamaterials
arxiv-2205-07084.creator: Carlo Rizza, Giuseppe Castaldi, Vincenzo Galdi
arxiv-2205-07084.description: Abstract We study a class of temporal metamaterials characterized by time-varying dielectric permittivity waveforms of duration much smaller than the characteristic wave-dynamical timescale. In the analogy between spatial and temporal metamaterials, such a short-pulsed regime can be viewed as the temporal counterpart of metasurfaces.

arxiv-2305-07665.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Affective Computing; Challenges, Trends, Applications, and Future Directions
arxiv-2305-07665.creator: Sitara Afzal, Haseeb Ali Khan, Imran Ullah Khan, Md. Jalil Piran, Jong Weon Lee
arxiv-2305-07665.description: Abstract As the name suggests, affective computing aims to recognize human emotions, sentiments, and feelings. There is a wide range of fields that study affective computing, including languages, sociology, psychology, computer science, and physiology. However, no research has ever been done to determine how machine learning (ML) and mixed reality (XR) interact together.

arxiv-2407-21145.title: The Hausdorff dimension of planar elliptic measures via quasiconformal mappings Thanks: Supported by the PIF UAB 2020/21 from the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, and by Generalitat de Catalunya’s Agency for Management of University and Research Grants (AGAUR) (2021 FI_B 00637 and 2023 FI-3 00151)
arxiv-2407-21145.creator: Ignasi Guillén-Mola
arxiv-2407-21145.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ignasi Guillén-Mola. In this paper, we obtain new bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of planar elliptic measure via the application of quasiconformal mappings, with these bounds depending solely on the ellipticity constant of the matrix. In fact, in our case studies, we find a quasiconformal mapping that relates the elliptic measure in a domain to the harmonic measure in its image domain, allowing us to deduce bounds for the dimension of the elliptic measure from the known results on the harmonic side.

arxiv-2409-20302.title: OM4OV: Leveraging Ontology Matching for Ontology Versioning
arxiv-2409-20302.creator: Kerry Taylor, Weiqing Wang
arxiv-2409-20302.description: Abstract Due to the dynamics of the Semantic Web, version control is necessary to manage changes in widely used ontologies. Despite the long-standing recognition of ontology versioning (OV) as a crucial component of efficient ontology management, many approaches treat OV as similar to ontology matching (OM) and directly reuse OM systems for OV tasks.

arxiv-2502-02010.title: A Steepest Gradient Method with Nonmonotone Adaptive Step-sizes for the Nonconvex Minimax and Multi-Objective Optimization Problems
arxiv-2502-02010.creator: Nguyen Duc Anh a and Tran Ngoc Thang a, ∗
arxiv-2502-02010.description: Abstract This paper proposes a new steepest gradient descent method for solving nonconvex finite minimax problems using non-monotone adaptive step sizes and providing proof of convergence results in cases of the nonconvex, quasiconvex, and pseudoconvex differentiate component functions. The proposed method is applied using a referenced-based approach to solve the nonconvex multiobjective programming problems.

arxiv-2507-20709.title: Preliminary orbits with over-determined systems of Keplerian conservation laws
arxiv-2507-20709.creator: C. Grassi, G. F. Gronchi
arxiv-2507-20709.description: Abstract We consider different choices of Keplerian conservation laws for the computation of preliminary orbits with two very short arcs (VSAs) of astrometric observations. In total we have 7 equations in 4 unknowns. Adding two auxiliary variables we can embed the full set of conservation laws into a polynomial system of 9 equations. This complete system generically has no solutions.

pmc-10710903.title: Inhaled Medication Errors During Hospitalization or on Hospital Discharge in Patients Living With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Literature Review
pmc-10710903.creator: Paul M Boylan, Macie J Gibbs, Katelyn N Helwig
pmc-10710903.description: Inhaled medications, including beta-agonists, muscarinic antagonists, and corticosteroids, are the backbone of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) treatment, and pharmacotherapy plans are frequently optimized during and following hospitalization. Clinical practice guidelines acknowledge that patients living with COPD may experience medication errors from inadequate inhaler technique or device faults, but inhaled medication errors within COPD pharmacotherapy plans remain unreported.

pmc-11464089.title: Solitary Renal Metastases From Stage IA Primary Lung Adenocarcinoma With Co‐Alteration of EGFR, RB1, and MAP3K1: A Case Report
pmc-11464089.creator: Zhu Qin, Chen Xin, He Zhenzhen, Xie Liang, Yi Wei, Li Shuben
pmc-11464089.description: We report a case of 59‐year‐old female with solitary bilateral renal metastases after surgery of stage IA primary lung adenocarcinoma who underwent next‐generation sequencing (NGS) of both lesions. The patient received right upper lobectomy and lymph node dissection, which revealed primary invasive lung adenocarcinoma (pT1cN0M0, stage IA3).

pmc-11516883.title: Polypharmacy and associated factors in the older population in Germany: Results Gesundheit 65+ study
pmc-11516883.creator: G Sarganas, D Grams, A Ordoñez-Cruickshank, J Fuchs, H Neuhauser, B Gaertner, P Thuermann
pmc-11516883.description: BackgroundPolypharmacy, the use of 5 or more medications simultaneously, favors the risk of adverse drug events, drug interactions, potentially inappropriate medication (PIM), hospitalizations, falls, frailty, and mortality. This analysis presents the prevalence of polypharmacy and associated factors in people aged 66+ years living in Germany.

pmc-11588970.title: Room-temperature mL-to-μL quantitative liquid concentration device for cyclone flow
pmc-11588970.creator: Hidekatsu Tazawa, Kazuma Mawatari
pmc-11588970.description: Highly sensitive quantitative analysis of liquids is required in various fields. Analytical instruments and devices such as chromatography, spectroscopic analysis, DNA sequencers, immunoassay, mass spectrometry, and microfluidic devices are utilized for this purpose. Typically, the sample volume is at the milliliter scale, while the analysis volume is at the microliter scale. Consequently, most of the sample is discarded.

pmc-11677924.title: Adipose Tissue as a Major Launch Spot for Circulating Extracellular Vesicle-Carried MicroRNAs Coordinating Tissue and Systemic Metabolism
pmc-11677924.creator: Paula Diez-Roda, Elena Perez-Navarro, Ruben Garcia-Martin
pmc-11677924.description: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), especially transported by extracellular vesicles (EVs), have recently emerged as major new participants in interorgan communication, playing an important role in the metabolic coordination of our tissues. Among these, adipose tissue displays an extraordinary ability to secrete a vast list of EV-carried miRNAs into the circulation, representing new hormone-like factors.

pmc-12693877.title: Deployment Challenges in Electromagnetic Wireless Nanosensor Networks
pmc-12693877.creator: Amani Bamuqabel, Saoucene Mahfoudh, Dionisis Kandris
pmc-12693877.description: Wireless nanosensor networks (WNSNs) are a future technology that will help transform many ideas into reality. Therefore, WNSNs must be properly set up to achieve their intended application goals during the deployment stage. An effective deployment protocol should ensure full coverage of the target area, continuous connectivity between nanosensors, and efficient energy consumption.

pmc-12714347.title: The Microbiota of Homemade Tepache Includes Antibiotic-Resistant Microorganisms
pmc-12714347.creator: Timothy Allshouse, Myleen Amendano, Becky Caruso, Realyn Del Campo, Gwen Murphy, Lauren Shaffer, Ethan Steinberg, Aidan Sullivan, Emily Stowe
pmc-12714347.description: Tepache is a traditional, homemade Mexican drink made by fermenting pineapple rinds. The natural probiotic bacteria in tepache are said to promote a healthy gut microbiome. This study assessed the microbial community in homemade tepache for diversity, survival in simulated gastric fluid, and antibiotic resistance.

pmc-12801168.title: Adherence to peripheral venous catheters’ guidelines by emergency nurses: A systematic review
pmc-12801168.creator: Joana Teixeira, Celeste Bastos, Maria do Rosário Pinto
pmc-12801168.description: BackgroundPeripheral intravenous catheters are widely used in emergency departments for intravenous treatment. However, peripheral intravenous catheter practices supported by the latest evidence remain suboptimal, negatively affecting patient outcomes.ObjectiveTo identify the determinants influencing adherence to peripheral intravenous catheter guidelines in the emergency department (the insertion technique, maintenance protocols, and timely removal) and to analyse strategies for improving adherence.

pmc-13113662.title: Antibiotic-Loaded PLA Composites for Local Prevention of Implant-Associated Infections: Comparative Evaluation Against Reference Strains and Clinical Isolates
pmc-13113662.creator: Anastassiya Khrustaleva, Azamat Yedrissov, Dmitriy Khrustalev, Irina Losseva, Alyona Lavrinenko, Artyom Savelyev, Vladimir Kazantsev, Marlen Kiikbayev, Polina Rusyaeva, Kristina Perepelitsyna, Aigerim Donenbaeva
pmc-13113662.description: Background/Objectives: Implant-associated infections remain among the most severe and clinically challenging complications in contemporary orthopedics, largely due to the formation of persistent bacterial biofilms and the limited penetration of systemically administered antibiotics into the tissue–implant interface. In this context, local antibacterial functionalization of implantable materials represents a promising strategy for the prevention of early infectious complications.

pmc-13486818.description: Neuroglial cysts, also known as glioependymal cysts, are rare benign congenital intracranial lesions of neuroectodermal origin. uslaw-usc-t26-s6201.title: 26 U.S.C. § 6201 — Assessment authority
uslaw-usc-t26-s6201.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s6201.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 63 (Assessment); Subchapter A (In General). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority of Secretary The Secretary is authorized and required to make the inquiries, determinations, and assessments of all taxes (including interest, additional amounts, additions to the tax, and assessable penalties) imposed by this title, or accruing under any former internal revenue.
